ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Fannie Lou Hamer

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mrs. Hamer is a 49-year-old community organizer with hypertension, type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease who comes for her yearly preventive visit two months after her four-month review. Her home blood pressure readings average 126/78. She takes her medicines each evening with her meal and has had no low blood sugar, dizziness or ankle swelling. SNAP and the energy assistance are in place, and the health center's van has brought her to every visit since the spring. Her legs and back still ache after long days, and acetaminophen helps. Her mood is steady and she is busy with organizing work. She asked what screening she needs and said plainly which examinations she would and would not agree to today. [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 2.1.1: Informed Consent (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026); Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Breast Cancer: Screening (2024); Cervical Cancer: Screening (2018); Colorectal Cancer: Screening (2021)

Follow-up: Mammogram in three weeks; stool test by mail; HIV and hepatitis C results at the October visit. Seven-month review in five weeks with the A1c, urine albumin, kidney function, influenza, COVID-19 and zoster vaccines. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-19: seven-month review: A1c, urine albumin, kidney function, seasonal and age-50 vaccines, screening results, and plans for the winter. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 25 minutes, with her consent. She wants to be told plainly what is wrong and what is proposed, and she wants no operation or procedure done to her without her own agreement, or, if she cannot speak, the agreement of the person she has named; she asked that this be written at the top of her plan, and it was. She wants full treatment for any illness that could be reversed. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and chose not to record other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
